x.description: The SOURCE tile of the transition - the door or warp tile you must already be standing next to. chestId.description: The container's published id, copied from `targetId` of the chestStoreTargets / chestRetrieveTargets row you mean. It already names the location, the tile and the chest type, so there is no separate `x`/`y` argument: the body re-derives the tile from this id and refuses `chest_target_changed` when no live container answers to it (removed, moved, or replaced by another chest type). A fridge is named by the same kind of id.

expectedQualifiedItemId.description: The item id to move, copied from `qualifiedItemId` of the chestStoreTargets row. There is no `slot`: the body takes the FIRST stack of this item id in the backpack and releases exactly that stack, and the receipt's `source_slot` names which one moved. Refused `item_not_owned_in_slot` when the backpack holds none of it by then.

There is no `slot`: the body takes the FIRST carried stack of this item id on arrival and ships exactly that stack, because the walk to a bin takes many ticks and a magnet pickup or a stack merge shifts slots on the way. expectedTargetId.description: The bin's published id, copied from `targetId` of the shippingBinTargets row. It already names the location and the bin's footprint, so the body re-resolves the live bin from it; a bin that has moved or been replaced is refused `shipping_bin_target_changed` instead of being retargeted onto whatever now stands there.
